title: Fuel and Throttle Component Locations — 5.0L
introduction:
The engine picture brings air control and fuel delivery into the same view, but they perform different jobs. I start at the throttle body at the front of the intake, then look along the fuel rails above the injectors. Match the circled callouts to the engine table to identify each component on this 5.0L arrangement.

The throttle body controls the air entering the engine. The rails distribute fuel, and the electrically controlled injectors meter it. Think of the rails as the supply plumbing and the injectors as the controlled outlets; identifying the plumbing is useful, but it cannot tell you whether an outlet is working correctly.

The transparent rendering lets you see components through the surrounding engine parts. It shows their relationship, not a ready-made access route. The separate cabin illustration and its own table locate the fuel pump driver module (FPDM) beneath the rear seat cushion on the left-hand side. Read that view independently from the engine callouts.

This reference gets you to the correct component name and location. It does not teach seat removal, electrical testing, fuel-pressure measurement or component replacement. Before any later work opens the fuel system, use the applicable pressure-release procedure: a fuel rail can remain pressurized after the engine stops.

edits.why: The engine qualifier selects the illustrated arrangement. Ti-VCT means twin independent variable camshaft timing; the view here identifies the throttle body and fuel-delivery components rather than the timing hardware.
FPDM means fuel pump driver module. Its separate cabin view places it beneath the rear seat cushion on the LH side; the location does not establish how to release the cushion or test the module.
